integrity: The proof first establishes a two-way equivalence between a two-piece max-min inradius division and two disjoint equal inballs. For an orthotope, ball centers lie in the eroded orthotope, reducing feasibility to a strictly decreasing quadratic diameter inequality. At a nonsaturated optimum, equality forces opposite eroded-box vertices and a unique separating tangent hyperplane. A standalone checker independently tests the quadratic profile, phase transition, cube and rectangle specializations, and deterministic numerical bisections; finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is for two successive-hyperplane pieces only. In the saturated orthotope regime the optimal value is exact but the optimizer family can be continuous. The two-equal-ball packing calculation is elementary and not claimed as new by itself; the scientific claim is the division-packing identity, its orthotope specialization, and the optimizer classification. A 2022 public conference abstract gives the earliest exact public day verified here and cites a 2021 preprint without an exact public day; no earlier exact public date is asserted.
title: Exact max-min inradius divisions of orthotopes
